reason: I’ll start with the fibroblast branch to work toward making supporting material outside cells.
expectation: I expect the timed conditions to guide some descendants toward fibroblasts, though further steps will likely be needed to make extracellular material.

alternatives.reason: The muscle branch also serves a goal, but I’ll follow the fibroblast branch first.

reaction: The unchanged DNA alongside active collagen genes makes the differentiation connection clear.
reason: I’ll continue the fibroblast branch toward extracellular supporting material.
expectation: I expect the cells to use the amino acids and collagen messages to make collagen protein, possibly requiring further processing or secretion.

reason: I’ll combine the fibroblasts with extracellular fluid to advance the supporting-material goal.
expectation: I expect collagen precursors to be secreted and processed outside the cells into supporting material.

alternatives.reason: I could begin the muscle branch, but I’ll continue the collagen pathway first.

effect: The collagen precursors were secreted and assembled into extracellular matrix, completing the supporting-material goal.
reaction: The distinction between living cells and the material they produce is clear and useful.
reason: The only available combination starts the remaining muscle-forming branch.
expectation: I expect the timed conditions to guide a separate subset of descendants toward muscle precursor cells.

effect: The muscle branch has committed cells with muscle-protein messages, but no mature fibres yet.
reaction: The contrast with collagen gene activity reinforces how the same DNA supports different cell roles.
reason: The only available combination uses amino acids to advance muscle-cell preparation.
expectation: I expect the cells to make muscle proteins from their RNA messages; further development may still be needed.

effect: The muscle cells made proteins from their selected messages and became myoblasts, completing the goal without yet forming mature fibres.
reaction: The distinction between separate precursors and a mature fibre is useful, and the shared amino-acid supply ties the two branches together.

mostWorthwhile.text: Making extracellular matrix was most worthwhile: the planned sequence connects secretion and assembly to the idea that tissue includes both cells and their surroundings.

leastWorthwhile.text: The second amino-acid combination felt somewhat repetitive after the collagen branch, though the different messages gave the repetition a teaching purpose.

surprise.text: The muscle branch stopped at separate, single-nucleus myoblasts rather than producing a mature fibre; that made the limits of the construction clear.

arbitrary.text: Combining fibroblasts with extracellular fluid is an abstract way to trigger secretion, but its purpose was clear from the supplied description. Nothing felt particularly arbitrary.

continue.text: Yes. I would be interested to see how the precursors develop and how cells and extracellular matrix form working tissues, although the fast menu made the choices fairly straightforward.
